raw: Act 2, Scene 4 — A Street

summary.en: Mercutio and Romeo trade jokes in the street. The Nurse comes, and Romeo tells her the plan: Juliet must come to the Friar's cell to marry him.

raw: Enter Benvolio and Mercutio.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Where the devil should this Romeo be? Came he not home tonight?

sentences.en: Where could this Romeo be?
Did he not come home tonight?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Not to his father’s; I spoke with his man.

sentences.en: He did not go to his father's house.
I spoke with his servant.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Why, that same pale hard-hearted wench, that Rosaline, torments him so
that he will sure run mad.

sentences.en: That same pale and hard-hearted girl, Rosaline, torments him so much.
She will surely make him go mad.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Tybalt, the kinsman to old Capulet, hath sent a letter to his father’s
house.

sentences.en: Tybalt, the relative of old Capulet, sent a letter to his father's house.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: A challenge, on my life.

sentences.en: It is a challenge, I swear it on my life.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Romeo will answer it.

sentences.en: Romeo will answer it.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Any man that can write may answer a letter.

sentences.en: Any man who can write can answer a letter.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Nay, he will answer the letter’s master, how he dares, being dared.

sentences.en: No, he will answer the man who wrote it, and show he dares when he is dared.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Alas poor Romeo, he is already dead, stabbed with a white wench’s black
eye; run through the ear with a love song, the very pin of his heart
cleft with the blind bow-boy’s butt-shaft. And is he a man to encounter
Tybalt?

sentences.en: Alas, poor Romeo.
He is already dead.
He was stabbed by a young woman's dark eyes.
A love song pierced his ears.
The arrow of the blind boy-god of love hit the very center of his heart.
Is he a man who can face Tybalt?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Why, what is Tybalt?

sentences.en: Why, what is so special about Tybalt?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
More than Prince of cats. O, he’s the courageous captain of
compliments. He fights as you sing prick-song, keeps time, distance,
and proportion. He rests his minim rest, one, two, and the third in
your bosom: the very butcher of a silk button, a duellist, a duellist;
a gentleman of the very first house, of the first and second cause. Ah,
the immortal passado, the punto reverso, the hay.

sentences.en: He is more than just a prince of cats.
He is a master of fancy fighting manners.
He fights as you sing music exactly from the page, keeping time and distance and proportion.
He pauses for a short beat—one, two—and the third is in your chest.
He can cut a single silk button off your shirt.
He is a skilled fighter and a duellist.
He is from the best fencing school and knows every rule for when to fight a duel.
Ah, those fancy Italian moves: the passado, the punto reverso, the hay!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: The what?

sentences.en: The what?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
The pox of such antic lisping, affecting phantasies; these new tuners
of accent. By Jesu, a very good blade, a very tall man, a very good
whore. Why, is not this a lamentable thing, grandsire, that we should
be thus afflicted with these strange flies, these fashion-mongers,
these pardon-me’s, who stand so much on the new form that they cannot
sit at ease on the old bench? O their bones, their bones!

sentences.en: A plague on these silly, show-off people with their fake accents!
They say things like, 'By Jesus, a very good sword, a very brave man, a very good whore!'
Is it not sad, old man?
We are bothered by these strange, annoying flies.
These are just people who follow new fashions.
They say 'pardon me' so much.
They care so much about the new style that they cannot sit comfortably on the old bench.
Oh, their bones, their bones!

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Here comes Romeo, here comes Romeo!

sentences.en: Here comes Romeo!
Here comes Romeo!

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Without his roe, like a dried herring. O flesh, flesh, how art thou
fishified! Now is he for the numbers that Petrarch flowed in. Laura, to
his lady, was but a kitchen wench,—marry, she had a better love to
berhyme her: Dido a dowdy; Cleopatra a gypsy; Helen and Hero hildings
and harlots; Thisbe a grey eye or so, but not to the purpose. Signior
Romeo, bonjour! There’s a French salutation to your French slop. You
gave us the counterfeit fairly last night.

sentences.en: He looks like a dried fish without its eggs.
Oh, flesh, how you have turned into fish!
Now he is ready for love poems like Petrarch's.
Compared with his lady, Petrarch's Laura was just a kitchen maid.
But Laura had a better poet to write about her.
Dido was a plain woman and Cleopatra was a gypsy.
Helen and Hero were common women.
Thisbe had nice grey eyes, but that is not important.
Mr. Romeo, bonjour!
That is a French hello for your baggy French pants.
You gave us the slip last night.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Good morrow to you both. What counterfeit did I give you?

sentences.en: Good morning to you both.
How did I trick you?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: The slip sir, the slip; can you not conceive?

sentences.en: The slip, sir, the slip.
Can you not understand?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Pardon, good Mercutio, my business was great, and in such a case as
mine a man may strain courtesy.

sentences.en: Forgive me, good Mercutio.
My business was very important.
In a case like mine, a man may forget his manners.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
That’s as much as to say, such a case as yours constrains a man to bow
in the hams.

sentences.en: That is like saying a case like yours makes a man weak in the knees.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Meaning, to curtsy.

sentences.en: Meaning, to curtsy.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Thou hast most kindly hit it.

sentences.en: You hit the mark perfectly.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: A most courteous exposition.

sentences.en: That was a very polite explanation.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Nay, I am the very pink of courtesy.

sentences.en: No, I am the perfect flower of politeness.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Pink for flower.

sentences.en: Pink, like the flower.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Right.

sentences.en: Right.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Why, then is my pump well flowered.

sentences.en: Then my shoe is well decorated with flowers.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Sure wit, follow me this jest now, till thou hast worn out thy pump,
that when the single sole of it is worn, the jest may remain after the
wearing, solely singular.

sentences.en: You are clever.
Follow this joke with me now.
Continue it until you have worn out your shoe.
When the single sole of it is worn, the joke will remain.
It will be unique and special.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O single-soled jest, solely singular for the singleness!

sentences.en: What a thin joke, as thin as a worn-out sole!

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Come between us, good Benvolio; my wits faint.

sentences.en: Come between us, good Benvolio.
My intelligence is failing.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Swits and spurs, swits and spurs; or I’ll cry a match.

sentences.en: Whip and spur your wits, or I will say I won!

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Nay, if thy wits run the wild-goose chase, I am done. For thou hast
more of the wild-goose in one of thy wits, than I am sure, I have in my
whole five. Was I with you there for the goose?

sentences.en: No, if your wits are on a wild-goose chase, I give up.
One of your wits has more wild goose in it than all five of mine.
Did I score a point with 'goose'?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Thou wast never with me for anything, when thou wast not there for the
goose.

sentences.en: You were never with me for anything unless you were acting like a goose.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: I will bite thee by the ear for that jest.

sentences.en: I will bite your ear for that joke.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Nay, good goose, bite not.

sentences.en: No, good goose, do not bite.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Thy wit is a very bitter sweeting, it is a most sharp sauce.

sentences.en: Your wit is a very sour apple.
It is a very sharp sauce.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: And is it not then well served in to a sweet goose?

sentences.en: Then isn't it the right sauce for a sweet goose?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
O here’s a wit of cheveril, that stretches from an inch narrow to an
ell broad.

sentences.en: Your wit is like soft leather.
It stretches from one inch to a whole yard wide.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I stretch it out for that word broad, which added to the goose, proves
thee far and wide a broad goose.

sentences.en: I stretch it for that word 'broad'.
Add it to 'goose', and it proves you are a big, broad goose.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Why, is not this better now than groaning for love? Now art thou
sociable, now art thou Romeo; now art thou what thou art, by art as
well as by nature. For this drivelling love is like a great natural,
that runs lolling up and down to hide his bauble in a hole.

sentences.en: Why, is this not better than groaning for love?
Now you are sociable and now you are Romeo.
Now you are what you are, by skill as well as by nature.
This silly love is like a big fool.
He runs around with his tongue out, looking for a hole to hide his stick in.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Stop there, stop there.

sentences.en: Stop there, stop there.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Thou desirest me to stop in my tale against the hair.

sentences.en: You want me to stop my tale against my will.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Thou wouldst else have made thy tale large.

sentences.en: You would have made your story much longer.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
O, thou art deceived; I would have made it short, for I was come to the
whole depth of my tale, and meant indeed to occupy the argument no
longer.

sentences.en: No, you are mistaken.
I wanted to make it short.
I had reached the deepest part of my story.
I really intended to stop talking about this topic.

raw: Enter Nurse and Peter.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Here’s goodly gear!
A sail, a sail!

sentences.en: Here comes something grand!
A ship, a ship!

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Two, two; a shirt and a smock.

sentences.en: Two, two: a man's shirt and a woman's dress.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Peter!

sentences.en: Peter!

speaker: PETER
raw: Anon.

sentences.en: Coming!

speaker: NURSE
raw: My fan, Peter.

sentences.en: My fan, Peter.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Good Peter, to hide her face; for her fan’s the fairer face.

sentences.en: Good Peter, give it to her so she can hide her face.
Her fan is prettier than her face.

speaker: NURSE
raw: God ye good morrow, gentlemen.

sentences.en: Good morning to you, gentlemen.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: God ye good-den, fair gentlewoman.

sentences.en: Good evening, beautiful lady.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Is it good-den?

sentences.en: Is it evening?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
’Tis no less, I tell ye; for the bawdy hand of the dial is now upon the
prick of noon.

sentences.en: It is no earlier, I tell you.
The naughty hand of the clock is now on the point of noon.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Out upon you! What a man are you?

sentences.en: Shame on you!
What kind of man are you?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: One, gentlewoman, that God hath made for himself to mar.

sentences.en: I am a man whom God made for himself to ruin.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
By my troth, it is well said; for himself to mar, quoth a? Gentlemen,
can any of you tell me where I may find the young Romeo?

sentences.en: Truly, that is well said.
'To ruin himself,' he says!
Gentlemen, can any of you tell me where I can find the young Romeo?

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I can tell you: but young Romeo will be older when you have found him
than he was when you sought him. I am the youngest of that name, for
fault of a worse.

sentences.en: I can tell you.
But young Romeo will be older when you find him than he was when you started looking.
I am the youngest Romeo, since there is no worse one.

speaker: NURSE
raw: You say well.

sentences.en: You say it well.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Yea, is the worst well? Very well took, i’faith; wisely, wisely.

sentences.en: So the worst is good?
Very well understood!
Wise, very wise.

speaker: NURSE
raw: If you be he, sir, I desire some confidence with you.

sentences.en: If you are he, sir, I want a private talk with you.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: She will endite him to some supper.

sentences.en: She will invite him to some supper.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: A bawd, a bawd, a bawd! So ho!

sentences.en: She is a pimp, a pimp, a pimp!
Tally-ho, I found one!

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What hast thou found?

sentences.en: What have you found?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
No hare, sir; unless a hare, sir, in a lenten pie, that is something
stale and hoar ere it be spent.

sentences.en: Not a rabbit, sir.
Unless it is an old rabbit in a pie, gone stale and gray before it is eaten.

raw: Sings.

sentences.en: Mercutio sings.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
An old hare hoar,
And an old hare hoar,
Is very good meat in Lent;
But a hare that is hoar
Is too much for a score
When it hoars ere it be spent.
Romeo, will you come to your father’s? We’ll to dinner thither.

sentences.en: An old hare that is stale is very good meat in Lent.
But a hare that becomes stale before it is eaten is not good for many people.
Romeo, will you go to your father's house?
We will go there for dinner.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I will follow you.

sentences.en: I will follow you.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Farewell, ancient lady; farewell, lady, lady, lady.

sentences.en: Goodbye, old lady.
Goodbye, lady, lady, lady.

raw: Exeunt Mercutio and Benvolio.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I pray you, sir, what saucy merchant was this that was so full of his
ropery?

sentences.en: Please tell me, sir, who was that rude fellow?
He was full of dirty jokes.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
A gentleman, Nurse, that loves to hear himself talk, and will speak
more in a minute than he will stand to in a month.

sentences.en: He is a gentleman, Nurse.
He loves to hear himself talk.
He will say more in one minute than he can stand for in a month.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
And a speak anything against me, I’ll take him down, and a were lustier
than he is, and twenty such Jacks. And if I cannot, I’ll find those
that shall. Scurvy knave! I am none of his flirt-gills; I am none of
his skains-mates.—And thou must stand by too and suffer every knave to
use me at his pleasure!

sentences.en: If he says anything against me, I will take him down.
I will do it even if he were stronger than he is, and twenty more like him.
And if I cannot, I will find people who can.
Nasty rascal!
I am not one of his loose girls.
I am not one of his gang.
And you must stand by and let every man use me as he likes!

speaker: PETER
raw:
I saw no man use you at his pleasure; if I had, my weapon should
quickly have been out. I warrant you, I dare draw as soon as another
man, if I see occasion in a good quarrel, and the law on my side.

sentences.en: I did not see any man use you at his pleasure.
If I had, my weapon would have come out quickly.
I promise you, I dare to draw as soon as another man does.
I do it when I see a good fight and the law is on my side.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Now, afore God, I am so vexed that every part about me quivers. Scurvy
knave. Pray you, sir, a word: and as I told you, my young lady bid me
enquire you out; what she bade me say, I will keep to myself. But first
let me tell ye, if ye should lead her in a fool’s paradise, as they
say, it were a very gross kind of behaviour, as they say; for the
gentlewoman is young. And therefore, if you should deal double with
her, truly it were an ill thing to be offered to any gentlewoman, and
very weak dealing.

sentences.en: Now, before God, I am so annoyed that every part of me shakes.
Nasty rascal!
Please, sir, listen to me for a moment.
As I told you, my young lady asked me to talk to you.
I will keep what she told me to say to myself.
But first let me tell you something.
If you lead her into a fool's paradise, as they say, it would be very bad behavior.
The lady is young, after all.
So if you trick her, it would be a terrible thing to do to any lady.
It would be a very weak way of acting.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Nurse, commend me to thy lady and mistress. I protest unto
thee,—

sentences.en: Nurse, give my regards to your lady.
I promise you—

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Good heart, and i’faith I will tell her as much. Lord, Lord, she will
be a joyful woman.

sentences.en: You are kind.
And I promise I will tell her that much.
Lord, she will be a happy woman.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What wilt thou tell her, Nurse? Thou dost not mark me.

sentences.en: What will you tell her, Nurse?
You are not paying attention to me.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I will tell her, sir, that you do protest, which, as I take it, is a
gentlemanlike offer.

sentences.en: I will tell her, sir, that you make a promise.
I think this is a gentlemanly offer.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Bid her devise
Some means to come to shrift this afternoon,
And there she shall at Friar Lawrence’ cell
Be shriv’d and married. Here is for thy pains.

sentences.en: Tell her to find a way to come for confession this afternoon.
There, at Friar Lawrence's cell, his little room, she will confess her sins and be married.
Here is a coin for your trouble.

speaker: NURSE
raw: No truly, sir; not a penny.

sentences.en: No, truly, sir; not a penny.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Go to; I say you shall.

sentences.en: Come on, I say you will take it.

speaker: NURSE
raw: This afternoon, sir? Well, she shall be there.

sentences.en: This afternoon, sir?
Well, she will be there.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
And stay, good Nurse, behind the abbey wall.
Within this hour my man shall be with thee,
And bring thee cords made like a tackled stair,
Which to the high topgallant of my joy
Must be my convoy in the secret night.
Farewell, be trusty, and I’ll quit thy pains;
Farewell; commend me to thy mistress.

sentences.en: And stay behind the wall of the church, dear Nurse.
My man will come to you within this hour.
He will bring ropes that look like a ladder.
In the secret night, they will carry me up to the top of my joy.
Goodbye. Be loyal, and I will pay you for your trouble.
Goodbye. Give my regards to your young lady.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Now God in heaven bless thee. Hark you, sir.

sentences.en: May God in heaven bless you.
Listen to me, sir.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: What say’st thou, my dear Nurse?

sentences.en: What do you say, my dear Nurse?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Is your man secret? Did you ne’er hear say,
Two may keep counsel, putting one away?

sentences.en: Is your man able to keep a secret?
Have you never heard the saying?
Two can keep a secret if one of them is gone.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I warrant thee my man’s as true as steel.

sentences.en: I promise you that my man is as true as steel.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Well, sir, my mistress is the sweetest lady. Lord, Lord! When ’twas a
little prating thing,—O, there is a nobleman in town, one Paris, that
would fain lay knife aboard; but she, good soul, had as lief see a
toad, a very toad, as see him. I anger her sometimes, and tell her that
Paris is the properer man, but I’ll warrant you, when I say so, she
looks as pale as any clout in the versal world. Doth not rosemary and
Romeo begin both with a letter?

sentences.en: Well, sir, my young lady is the sweetest girl.
Lord, Lord!
When she was a small child, she was a cute thing.
There is a nobleman in town named Paris.
He would like to marry her.
But she, dear soul, would rather see a toad.
She would rather see a real toad than see him.
I make her angry sometimes.
I tell her that Paris is the better man for her.
But I promise you, when I say this, she looks very pale.
She looks as pale as any cloth in the world.
Don't rosemary and Romeo both begin with the same letter?

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Ay, Nurse; what of that? Both with an R.

sentences.en: Yes, Nurse; what about that?
Both start with an R.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Ah, mocker! That’s the dog’s name. R is for the—no, I know it begins
with some other letter, and she hath the prettiest sententious of it,
of you and rosemary, that it would do you good to hear it.

sentences.en: Ah, you mocker!
That is the dog's sound.
R is for the—no, I know it begins with another letter.
She has the prettiest sayings about you and rosemary.
It would do you good to hear it.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Commend me to thy lady.

sentences.en: Give my regards to your lady.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Ay, a thousand times. Peter!

sentences.en: Yes, a thousand times.
Peter!

raw: Exit Romeo.

speaker: PETER
raw: Anon.

sentences.en: Coming!

speaker: NURSE
raw: Before and apace.

sentences.en: Walk ahead of me, and quickly.

raw: Exeunt.
